hyp: Bibimbap is a bowl of warm rice piled with seasoned vegetables, beef, and a fried egg. The Korean chili paste makes it mildly spicy, but you can ask for less. Give it a good mix with your spoon before you dig in. It has egg and soy, and most places do a meat-free version if you ask. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Bulgogi is thin slices of beef marinated in sweet soy sauce with garlic and sesame oil, then grilled until tender. There's no heat to it at all. It's sweet and savory. Eat it straight with rice or wrap a piece in lettuce with garlic. It has soy and sesame in it, and the soy sauce may bring gluten. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with a restaurant about allergies.

떡볶이 is chewy rice cakes and fish cakes simmered in a thick sweet chili sauce a street food favorite be warned it's properly spicy so ask for a milder version if you're not used to heat eat it straight from the pan while it's hot using a fork or a toothpick it has gluten and soy in it this is general info not medical advice check with the restaurant about allergies

Kimchi jjigae is a bubbling stew of aged kimchi, pork, and tofu in a tangy broth. The kimchi and chili flakes give it a solid kick. It comes in a shared pot, so ladle some into your own bowl and eat it with rice. It has soy in it, the broth sometimes has fish or seafood, and the pork version isn't halal or kosher. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

된장찌개 is a hearty stew of fermented soybean paste with tofu, zucchini, potato, and mushrooms. It isn't spicy at all, deep and savory, a little funky from the fermentation. Eat it hot, putting both the broth and the vegetables over rice. It has soy in it and is vegetarian if the stock has no meat or seafood. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Samgyeopsal is thick slices of plain pork belly that you grill yourself at the table. The meat isn't spicy though the dipping paste that comes with it is. Wrap a slice in a lettuce leaf with garlic and a dab of that paste. It has soy in it and it's pork so skip it if you avoid either. This is general info not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Kalbitang is beef short ribs simmered slowly into a clear soup with radish and glass noodles. There's no heat at all, just a light savory broth seasoned with salt and garlic. Put the tender meat off the ribs with your spoon and sip the broth as you go. It's mostly free of common allergens, but the soy sauce is worth asking about. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Mul naengmyeon is chewy buckwheat noodles in an icy tangy beef broth with cucumber, pear, and a boiled egg. It's not spicy, just cold and refreshing, which is why it's a summer favorite. Cut the noodles with the scissors they bring you, then add mustard and vinegar to taste. It has egg, and the noodles usually have wheat flour in them. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Bibim naengmyeon is chewy buckwheat noodles tossed in a sweet chili sauce and served cold with no broth. It's properly spicy. All that heat sits right on the noodles. Mix it thoroughly before you eat so the sauce coats everything. And add a splash of vinegar if you like. It has egg, soy, and gluten in it. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Japchae is glass noodles stir-fried with beef, spinach, carrots, and mushrooms. Glossy and a little sweet. There's no heat to it, just soy sauce and sesame oil. It's served warm or at room temperature. Eaten with chopsticks as a side or a light main. It has soy and sesame, and a version without beef is common. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Gimbap is rice and fillings rolled in dried seaweed and sliced into bite-sized pieces. There's no heat to it. It's mild and savory. Pick the slices up with your hands or chopsticks. You don't need a dipping sauce. It has egg and gluten. Sometimes tuna or ham and vegetarian versions are easy to find. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Sundubu jjigae is a bubbling stew of soft tofu in a bright red broth with a raw egg cracked in on top. It's properly spicy from the chili flakes and chili oil. Stir the egg in as soon as it arrives so it cooks in the broth, then eat with rice. It has soy and egg and often shellfish or pork. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergy.

Samgyetang is a whole young chicken stuffed with rice, garlic, and ginseng, then slow-boiled into a nourishing soup. It isn't spicy, the broth is clear and mild. Season the broth with salt and pepper, then put the chicken apart with your spoon. It has gluten from the glutinous rice, but is otherwise free of common allergens. This is general info, not medical advice check with the restaurant about allergies.

Jeyukbokkeum is thinly sliced pork stir-fried in a sweet chili marinade with garlic and ginger, a home-style favorite. It's properly spicy from the chili paste. Eat it with rice or wrap a bite in lettuce with a little rice. It has soy in it and it's pork, so skip it if you avoid that. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Kongnamul gukbap is rice in a light bean sprout broth. Gentle food and a known hangover cure. It comes mild, though you can add chili flakes or paste if you want. Eat it hot, spooning the rice, and sprouts up with the broth. It's mostly free of common allergens, though the broth may use seafood stock. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Mandu are Korean dumplings filled with meat, vegetables, or kimchi, and they come steamed, fried, or boiled in soup. They aren't spicy. Dip them in soy sauce mixed with vinegar and chili flakes, and eat them while they're hot. They have gluten and soy in them, and often pork. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Bibim guk is thin meat noodle sauce in a sweet chili sauce with cucumber and boiled egg. Serve cold. It's properly spicy with vinegar and sugar cutting through the chili paste. Mix it thoroughly before you eat so the sauce holds every strand of noodle. It has gluten, soy, and egg in it. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Tteokguk is thinly sliced rice cakes in a clear beef or anchovy broth. The soup Koreans eat on New Year's Day. It isn't spicy. Eat it hot with a spoon. It usually comes garnished with strips of egg and dry seaweed. It has gluten from the rice cakes and egg. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Sujebi is hand-torn pieces of dough simmered in a savory broth with potato, zucchini, and onion, rustic home cooking. It isn't spicy, just mild and comforting. Eat the soft dough and broth together while it's hot, much like a noodle soup. It has gluten, and the broth often has shellfish in it. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Mulhoe is raw fish and vegetables served in an icy, tangy broth, refreshing and a summer favorite. It's mildly spicy from the chili and vinegar in the broth. Many people pour the broth over rice at the end to finish the meal off. It has raw fish and soy in it. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Tofu kimchi is warm slices of boiled tofu served next to stir-fried kimchi, a favorite with drinks. It's mildly spicy. The kimchi carries the heat and the tofu cools it down. Put a bit of kimchi on a slice of tofu and eat them together. It has soy in it and sometimes pork. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Gyeranjjim is steamed egg, fluffy and souffle-like, usually brought to the table bubbling in a hot stone pot as a side dish. It isn't spicy, soft and savory is the whole idea. Spoon it straight from the pot and mix it with rice if you like. It's egg, so avoid it if you're allergic. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with a restaurant about allergies.

Bopchang jeongol is a hot pot of beef or pork intestines simmered at the table with vegetables, tofu, and glass noodles. The broth is chili-based and properly spicy. Wait for it to finish simmering, then serve yourself into a small bowl. It has soy in it, and it's awful, so it won't suit everyone. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Yukgaejang is a hearty beef soup with shredded meat, bean sprouts, and fern shoot. It's properly spicy. There's a good amount of chili oil in the broth. Eat it hot with rice and mix the rice straight in if you like. It's beef-based and mostly free of common allergens, though soy sauce usually goes in. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Kalguksu is hand-cut wheat noodles in a warm broth with zucchini, potato, and scallion. It isn't spicy, just mild and comforting. Eat the noodles and broth together with a spoon and chopsticks while it's hot. It has gluten, and the broth is often made with anchovy stock. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Chanchi guksu is thin wheat noodles in a light warm broth. A dish traditionally served at celebrations. It isn't spicy at all. Eat it while it's hot and stir in a little soy sauce or chili flakes if you want more flavor. It has gluten, egg, and anchovy in the broth. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Sundae is Korean blood sausage pig intestine stuffed with glass noodles and sticky rice. It isn't spicy on its own, though the dipping salt or sauce often is. Dip the slices in salt or chili paste. It usually comes with liver and other offal. It has gluten and it's pork, so skip it if you avoid pork or offal. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Jokbal is pig trotters braised for hours in soy sauce with ginger, garlic, and warm spices, then sliced. It isn't spicy, though a spicy dipping sauce sometimes comes alongside. Dip a slice in the sauce and wrap it in lettuce or perilla leaf with garlic and chili. It has soy in it, and it's pork. This is general info, not medical advice check with the restaurant about allergies.

Bossam is tender boiled pork belly served with lettuce, fresh kimchi, and a savory dipping paste. The pork isn't spicy, but the kimchi and chili sauce beside it are. Wrap a slice with kimchi and a dab of paste in a lettuce leaf and eat it in one bite. It has soy and shrimp from the kimchi and its pork. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

nakji bokkeum is fresh octopus stir-fried with vegetables in a fierce chili sauce chewy and seriously hot this one is very spicy go carefully if you are not used to it eat it with rice to take the edge off and keep a cold drink nearby it has octopus and soy in it so it's out if you avoid seafood this is general info not medical advice check with the restaurant about allergies

아귀찜 is monkfish and bean sprouts braised together in a thick, garlicky chili sauce meant for sharing. It's very spicy, so pace yourself. Everyone eats from the middle of the table. Use your chopsticks to pick out the fish and sprout. It has fish and soy in it, so it's out if you avoid seafood. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Maeuntang is a fiery fish stew often made from what's left after sashimi with radish and tofu. It's very spicy. There's a lot of chili in that broth. Eat it hot with rice, spooning up both the fish and the broth. It has fish and soy in it, so it's out if you avoid seafood. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Gamjajeon is a crispy pancake of grated potato, fried in oil with just a pinch of salt, simple and satisfying. It isn't spicy at all. Cut it into wedges and dip them in the soy vinegar sauce. There's not much in it that causes allergies, but the dipping sauce has soy. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

tteokgalbi is seasoned minced beef and pork shaped to a patty and grilled a korean hamburger steak there's no heat to it just a sweet soy glaze eat it with a knife and fork or chopsticks alongside rice and vegetables it has soy and sesame in it plus beef and pork this is general info not medical advice check with a restaurant about allergies

Cheonggukjang is a stew of fast-fermented soybeans famous for its strong smell and its rich savory taste. It's only mildly spicy. The punch is in the aroma, not the heat. Eat it hot with rice. The smell is stronger than the flavor, so it's worth trying with an open mind. It has soy in it. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Galchijorim is hair tail fish braised with radish in a spicy soy sauce rich and savory. It's properly spicy. Eat the fish carefully with your chopsticks. There are small bones along with the radish and rice. It has fish and soy in it. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Dongtaejjigae is a stew of frozen perlac simmered with tofu, radish, and scallion in a chili broth. It's properly spicy and warms you right through. Eat it hot with rice, spooning up both the fish and the broth. It has fish and soy in it. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Gamjatang is a stew of pork spine, bones, and potatoes, slow cooked until the meat falls off the bone. The chili broth runs deep red and is fairly hot. Pick the meat off the bones with your chopsticks, hands are fine too, and eat it with rice. It has soy in it and is pork. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Galbijjim is beef short ribs braised slowly in sweet soy sauce with chestnuts, carrots, and radish until they fall off the bone. There's no heat to it. It's sweet and savory. Eat the meat with chopsticks alongside rice and the braised vegetables. It has soy in it and it's beef. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

해물파전 is a creepy pancake packed with scallions, squid, shrimp, and mussels. What Koreans reach for on a rainy day, usually with rice wine. It isn't spicy. Peel or cut it into pieces and dip them in the soy vinegar sauce that comes with it. It has gluten, egg, and shellfish in it. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with a restaurant about allergies.

Galbi is beef short ribs in a sweet soy marinade grilled right at your table until the edges caramelize. There's no heat to it. Sweet and smoky is the idea. Grill it, then wrap a slice in lettuce with garlic and a dab of savory paste. It has soy in it and it's beef. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Kongguksu is wheat noodles in a chilled, creamy soybean broth topped with cucumber and sesame seeds. It isn't spicy. It's cold and nutty, made for hot weather. Add a pinch of salt or sugar to taste. Then eat the noodles cold with the broth. It has soy, gluten, and sesame in it. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with a restaurant about allergies.

Yukhoe is Korean beef tartare. Raw beef seasoned with sesame oil, sugar, and garlic with an egg yolk. It isn't spicy. Mix the yolk through the beef before you eat. Take a slice of tartare with it. It has egg and sesame and the beef is raw. Tell your server if that's okay. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergy.

간장게장 is raw crab marinated in soy sauce, so good with rice that Koreans call it the rice thief. It isn't spicy, the brine is savory rather than hot. Suck the meat and roll from the shell, then spoon rice into the empty shell. It has crab and soy in it, and the crab is raw. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Yangnyeom Gejang is raw crab marinated in a sweet chili sauce, the fiery cousin of the soy-marinated version. It's properly spicy. Eat the meat and roll with rice and mix whatever sauce is left in the shell into your rice. It has crab and soy in it, and the crab is raw. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Dakgalbi is diced chicken stir-fried at your table with cabbage, rice cakes, and sweet potato in a chili sauce. It's properly spicy. It's cooked and shared on one big pan, and most people finish by mixing fried rice into whatever sauce is left. It has gluten from the rice cakes and soy. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Jjimdak is chicken braised with glass noodles, potatoes, and carrots in a sweet soy sauce. There is a little chili in there, but it's only mildly spicy. Share it from the middle of the table, eating the chicken, vegetables, and noodles together. It has soy and gluten in it. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Kimchi bokkeumbap is rice stir-fried with chopped kimchi, usually with a fried egg on top. It's mildly spicy. The heat comes from the kimchi itself. Break the egg and mix it through the rice before you eat. Some people add seaweed flakes or cheese. It has egg and soy, and often ham or pork. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

오징어볶음 is squid stir-fried with onion, carrot, and scallion in a sweet chili sauce. Chewy and full of flavor. It's properly spicy. Eat it with rice to balance the heat. It usually comes with a bowl of soup on the side. It has squid and soy in it. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Sundaeguk is a hearty soup of pork bone broth with blood sausage and cuts of pork offal. It arrives mild, though most people stir in chili at the table. Season it with salt and chili to taste, then eat it with rice. It has gluten and it's pork, so skip it if you avoid pork or offal. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.
